questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power does the front brake provide?

options.text: About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent
100 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes so both apply when you use either brake lever.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter and applies the brake when you downshift.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a switch on the handlebar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes so both apply when you use either brake lever.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes apply. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: What following distance should you normally maintain?

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance when conditions are poor.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when it is raining?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane
Pull off to the side of the road until the rain stops
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
Increase your speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
questions.explanation: When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Oil from cars sits on the pavement and makes it very slippery when wet. The left tire track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, at what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is a person age 21 or older considered legally intoxicated?

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.06 percent
0.08 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and unsafe to ride a motorcycle while intoxicated.

questions.question: What should you do when taking a long trip?

options.text: Try to minimize the number of rest breaks
Use artificial stimulants like caffeine if you feel drowsy
Dress warmly to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain
Plan to ride more than 12 hours a day

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain
questions.explanation: To prevent fatigue on a long trip, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take a rest break every two hours. Avoid artificial stimulants like caffeine because you will become extremely tired when they wear off.

questions.question: What should you do when a vehicle tries to pass you from behind?

options.text: Move to the center portion of the lane
Move to the left portion of the lane
Move to the right portion of the lane
Not worry about which portion of the lane you are using

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center portion of your lane. Staying too close to the passing vehicle increases the risk of a collision.

questions.question: If the rear tire locks on a surface with good traction, what should you do?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake
Keep it locked until you completely stop
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you completely stop
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear brake on a surface with good traction, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can still steer your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: What can cause a wobble or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars?

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure
Brakes that are not working properly
A balanced load
Excessive wind

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure
questions.explanation: Most wobbles are caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: What guarantees that another driver sees you?

options.text: Eye contact
Using a turn signal
Following another vehicle
Nothing

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. Assume that if another vehicle can enter your path, it will.

questions.question: When looking through a turn to see where you are going, you should:

options.text: Turn just your head.
Turn your head and shoulders.
Turn just your shoulders.
Turn your entire body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: It takes up minimal space on the highway.
The group is easy to see.
The group is unlikely to be split up.
The riders will get to their destination more quickly in a close group than in a spread out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: The riders will get to their destination more quickly in a close group than in a spread out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a close group uses less road space, is easier for others to see, and keeps the group together at traffic lights and during passes. Close riding does not make you arrive faster.

questions.question: To work well, an eye or face shield must have all of the following qualities, except:

options.text: The ability to fasten securely.
Be too tight to allow sunglasses or eyeglasses to be worn.
Be free of scratches.
Allow clear views to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be too tight to allow sunglasses or eyeglasses to be worn.
questions.explanation: An effective eye or face shield must be free of scratches, fasten securely, allow clear side views, let air flow to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: If your front tire locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the brake engaged until you come to a full stop.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.
Release the brake lever and use only the rear brake.
Release the brake lever until the tire regains traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the brake lever until the tire regains traction.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake lever until the tire regains traction. Then apply the brake again.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, ride on the left side of your lane because:

options.text: The right side could be slippery.
It gives you the best chance to see hazards in the next lane.
People don't usually expect to be passed on their left.
It places you in the rearview mirror of the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you the best chance to see hazards in the next lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left part of your lane when preparing to pass. This position increases what you can see ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If you must brake while in a curve, you should:

options.text: Brake more gradually than you would on a straightaway.
Brake as hard as you would on a straightaway.
Wait until you are not in the curve to brake.
Only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gradually than you would on a straightaway.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when leaning than when upright. Try to straighten your motorcycle before braking. If you must brake in a curve, apply the brakes more gently than on a straight road.

questions.question: When you must both brake and swerve to avoid a sudden hazard, you should:

options.text: Perform one action, then the other.
Perform both actions at the same time and apply extra braking pressure.
Perform both actions at the same time, but mainly focus on swerving.
Not perform either action.

questions.correctAnswerText: Perform one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: You need good grip to swerve safely. Do not brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, perform one action first, then the other.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: Just behind the leader.
In the front of the group.
At the tail end of the group.
Beside the lead rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way they won't fall behind, and experienced riders can watch them from the back.

questions.question: Which of the following helps you ride safely on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Using only the front brake
Using both brakes
Using the center lane
Maintaining or increasing your speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and use both brakes. Avoid sudden movements. Stay out of the center lane and follow tire tracks left by cars. Watch for hazards like oil spots and loose gravel.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your reaction time to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: Why should you practice using convex mirrors if your motorcycle has them?

options.text: Most people are not used to using mirrors.
They make objects look farther away than they actually are.
They make objects look closer than they actually are.
It is hard to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects look farther away than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors do. They also make objects appear farther away than they really are. Practice using them so you get comfortable with how they work.

questions.question: How do you achieve maximum braking power in a straight line?

options.text: Use the rear brake only.
Use the front brake only.
Use both brakes.
Use the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Maximum braking power comes from fully applying both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time.
Always brake first, then swerve.
Try to use only the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, do them one at a time. Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting the animal.
Change lanes as quickly as possible.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Avoid hitting an animal if you can do so safely. However, if you are in traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane to miss a small animal could cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another car.
